tei:titleStmt.tei:title: Am Todestage des Gedaljahu. Ẓom Gedalja
[Prayer] on the Day of the Assassination of Gedalyahu (צוֹם גְּדַלְיָה), by Yehoshua Heshil Miro (1829)

tei:div.tei:head: Am Todestage des Gedaljahu. Ẓom Gedalja

tei:lg.tei:l: On the day of the death of Gedalyahu. Tsōm Gedalyah.

With deep sadness we remember today the time when our ancestors were subjugated by Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, and mostly driven out of their country. All-just and gracious God, you have preserved your word for us through the prophets, so that we may learn how obeying you is life and salvation; how every apostasy from your commandments, every rebellion against those who teach on behalf of your name, is sin and produces misfortune.

The pious Gedalyahu, who, according to the teachings of the prophet Jeremiah, instructed our ancestors to remain in their country and to obey the laws of the conqueror until the mercy of God would bring them better times, became a victim of the rage of wild zealots, who put more trust in their own wisdom, in their own strength than in God. Countless are the sad consequences of that terrible crime, and not without influence on later generations. Therefore, O God, grant that this reminder may be a warning to us to always obey the commandments of your faithful teachers and their counsel, to always be faithful subjects of the authority that is set over us. For nothing happens without your will, Lord, and even the smallest office is not granted without your election or consent.
The heart of the king, however, is like a stream of water; you direct it according to your will. So then you will always guide the heart of our rulers to mercy, that they may do us good. Amen.

tei:note.tei:p: On the second day of the month Tishrei, or for us the day after Rosh Hashanah, see Appendix.
